event: PHP Foundation researchers find a theoretical flaw in PHP but cannot work out how an attacker could use it
PHP Foundation accepted into OpenAI's Patch the Planet initiative (frontier AI to find and fix flaws in popular software)
Calif, part of the project, finds a serious flaw in PHP; researchers at OpenAI and Wiz find it shortly after
PHP Foundation works with the companies on a patch, planned for release in late October
Coordinated disclosure breaks down ('worked well until two days ago', per the PHP Foundation as quoted by the BBC): basic details leak on social media; Calif 'mistakenly published a video'
note: date inferred from 'two days ago' in a 22 Oct post

event: BBC opens its live page: governments and companies rush to protect websites
BBC reports the NSA's cyber division post on X: prepare 'for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities'; take systems offline if an immediate update is not feasible
note: time is the BBC post, not the NSA post

event: Ryan Austin (Calif) on Radio 4 Today: no evidence of exploitation yet ('Not at the moment')
